mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST QoQ change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate increase of at least 0.4 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >= 0.4pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production (INDPRO) decline of more than 1% from the previous month, sustained for two consecutive months, indicates supply-side contraction, which raises input costs and reduces profit expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of at least 0.3 percentage points in the federal funds rate and a monthly increase of at least 0.5% in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) signals a monetary policy lag with inflationary pressure, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change < -0.3pp AND CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both triggers are met (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase of at least 1% in real personal income (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening household balance sheets and higher consumption potential, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 5% for four consecutive months in a late-cycle context signals labor market tightness, which boosts wage inflation and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as profit margins compress.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% for four consecutive months AND regime is late-cycle
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 5% for four months in a late-cycle regime.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline of at least 2% in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which directly reduces corporate revenues and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes.
